summary: What you pay for health insurance, a Central Government Health Scheme or notified scheme contribution, or a preventive health check-up is deducted within limits: one limit for yourself, your spouse and dependant children, and a separate one for your parents, each larger for a senior citizen's insurance. Medical expenditure counts only for a senior citizen who has no health insurance. Check-ups for everyone together share one small limit, and are the only payment that may be in cash. A premium paid in advance for several years is spread across them. Only the old regime allows it.

routes.name: Yourself, your spouse and dependant children
routes.description: Insurance, a scheme contribution or a check-up, and an uninsured senior's medical expenditure, within the family's limits.

routes.name: Your parents
routes.description: Their insurance or check-up, and an uninsured senior parent's medical expenditure, within the parents' limits.

routes.name: A senior citizen in the family
routes.description: Insurance for a senior citizen in the family counts up to the higher limit.

routes.name: A senior citizen parent
routes.description: Insurance for a senior citizen parent counts up to the higher limit.

routes.name: Preventive health check-ups
routes.description: Check-ups for the family and parents together count within one small limit, which may be paid in cash.

disqualifiers.description: Not available in the default regime.
A payment other than for a check-up was made in cash.
Medical expenditure on a senior citizen whose health was insured in the year does not count.
A health scheme contribution for a parent does not count; for parents only insurance and check-ups do.
A single premium covering both a senior citizen and someone who is not is not computed.
